addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# LiveSpec vNext — consolidated master roadmap (external draft)
2	
3	Status: read-only synthesis, 2026-08-13. This is not a LiveSpec source of truth and must not be committed into the LiveSpec repository as another plan. It exists to prepare one coordinated update of the canonical product documents after owner acceptance.
4	
5	## Current verified state
6	
7	- Repository: `/Users/sashaabramovich/live-spec`
8	- `main` at `2718c69`, ahead of `origin/main` by 6 commits.
9	- Focused fast lane: `tests/test_guardrails_unit.py + tests/test_traceability.py` — 209 passed.
10	- Recent changes established: external product-prover adapter and bare-checkout contract; fast guardrail unit lane; prose/scoped changes no longer owe a fresh review record.
11	- Protected uncommitted work remains in `.live-spec/PROBLEMS.md`, `.live-spec/culling-plan-v3-2026-08-10.md`, and `docs/PROGRESS.md`.
12	- Old P2 worktree/branch remains unmerged and is not a source for vNext.
13	
14	## Finding
15	
16	The intended product is not missing. It already exists, dispersed across the product spec, architecture, roadmap, decisions, skills, profiles, hooks, and tests:
17	
18	- chat wish intake and durable queue rows;
19	- a work board with backlog/inception/ready/in-work/done, readable cards, task history, lanes, worktrees, estimates and actuals;
20	- personal and host profiles, project kinds, layers, proof kinds, onboarding and adoption;
21	- alternate routes for feature, bug, refactor, documentation and feedback;
22	- spec → prover → architecture → prover → matrix → tests → code traceability;
23	- agent cards, zones, ownership, dependency graph, isolated worktrees and one-pen integration;
24	- gates, fallback, install/sync, recovery, release and push controls.
25	
26	The defect is composition: these capabilities are fused into a 64 KB always-read base skill, other large skills, global hooks, and several competing status/history surfaces. vNext should replace the always-on control layer, not discard the capabilities or their machinery.
27	
28	## Target architecture
29	
30	1. **Thin router — always loaded.** Reads only the minimum user/project selectors, classifies answer versus work, determines task type and reach, and returns route, owner, execution policy, required proof and fallback.
31	2. **User policy — on demand.** Budget/capacity, autonomy, approval thresholds, communication preferences and reporting density.
32	3. **Project policy — on demand.** Project kind, stack, layers, proof kinds, sources of truth, install/release policy and available routes.
33	4. **Route catalogue — on demand.** Local change, local bug, cross-cutting feature, decision, debt, documentation/publish, feedback and project-kind-specific quality routes.
34	5. **Execution scheduler — on demand.** Computes agent count and model tier from budget, independent reach/write sets, worktrees, dependencies and shared resources. No permanent three-agent ceiling. One-pen and conflict guarantees remain.
35	6. **Evidence layer.** Existing specs, architecture, matrix, tests, prover records and commits remain the sources of contract and proof. Task state points to them and never restates them.
36	7. **Human visibility.** The existing work-board capability is implemented as a readable, derived/on-demand view over the canonical queue and evidence. It is not a new competing feature list or an always-read session document.
37	8. **Adaptive relationship policy — on demand.** Existing founding, adoption, profiles and the settings card become a progressive learning loop. Session observations remain ephemeral; only the person's words or individually accepted proposals become durable settings. The system starts useful work immediately and asks when uncertainty changes safety, cost or outcome.
38	9. **Estimator and calibration — on demand.** The existing work-board estimate/actual contract learns distributions by task type, reach, route and project. It returns a range and confidence with its evidence, freezes the estimate at take-up, records actual and end-to-end time at close, and recalibrates without rewriting history.
39	
40	## Capability groups
41	
42	| Group | Existing material to retain | vNext change |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| Intake and durable routing | wish/feedback intake, queue, inbox, decisions | thin pre-rulebook router; answer/no-work exit; one home per work item |
45	| Work graph and board | ROADMAP row 166/566, Requirement 309, work-board architecture target | readable derived board; inception; dependencies; collapsible details/history; no third feature map |
46	| Profiles and onboarding | settings ladder, personal/host profiles, project.kind/layers/proofs, founding/adoption, settings card | progressive discovery; observed/inferred/confirmed/revoked distinction; compact confirmed selectors; privacy and retention; adapt only inside consented bounds |
47	| Route catalogue | existing nine-station software pipeline and bug/refactor/docs shortcuts | executable/selectable route map rather than duplicated prose |
48	| Scheduler, estimates and agents | dependency graph, zones, agent cards, worktrees, lane opening, one pen, work-board estimate/actual fields | calibrated ranges by task class/reach/route/project; dynamic capacity by budget/reach/resources; model/skill assignment; shared-resource reservations |
49	| Traceability and quality | spec/architecture/matrix/test mappings, prover, design/text passes | preserve as compatibility oracle; load only the proof module required by the route |
50	| Lifecycle operations | gates, fallback, install/sync, CI, push, release, recovery | explicit route riders and conservative fallback; no universal review/full-suite ceremony |
51	
52	Later selectable product-quality modules remain in scope: feature-fit, visitor/feel validation, default expiry, consequence-first decisions, feedback measurement/A-B and project-kind-specific design/proof passes.
53	
54	## Compatibility ledgers required before cutover
55	
56	### Product parity
57	
58	`old capability → canonical source → vNext module/route → proof → retained | deferred | deprecated`
59	
60	### Operational parity
61	
62	`old mechanism → trigger → required state → owner → execution → verification → failure fallback → vNext equivalent → proof → retained | deferred | deprecated`
63	
64	No capability or mechanism is removed as a duplicate. `deprecated` requires an explicit owner decision. `deferred` continues to use the old LiveSpec route.
65	
66	The ledgers record proof state as `specified → implemented → tested → installed → invoked → evidence current`. A green string test does not prove an exercised mechanism.
67	
68	## Canonical-amendment rule
69	
70	There will be no parallel vNext product specification. This roadmap is an external migration worksheet only. Accepted behavior is amended in the existing canonical homes:
71	
72	- adaptive onboarding extends the existing founding, personal-profile, project-kind and settings-card requirements and their current architecture nodes;
73	- estimates extend the existing work-board statement, estimate/actual and delivery-trail clauses rather than creating an estimator specification beside them;
74	- work-graph schema and history extend the existing work-board requirement and node;
75	- legacy-host conversion extends the existing catch-up/adoption/migration requirements and `MIGRATION.md`;
76	- routing extends the existing door, kind, footprint and reach contracts;
77	- documentation structure belongs in the existing document/surface contracts;
78	- skill extraction is an architecture/install/release change and changes the product spec only where user-visible guarantees change.
79	
80	Every accepted change lands as one coordinated delta: product promise first, then architecture owner/seams, matrix proof, red-first tests, implementation and ROADMAP status. Existing anchors are retained or explicitly migrated; they are not copied into a second namespace.
81	
82	## Prioritized roadmap
83	
84	### R0 — stop drift and establish the migration baseline
85	
86	- Freeze new pruning, skill extraction and guardrail growth except blockers for the migration itself.
87	- Preserve the six current commits and the three protected dirty documents.
88	- Resolve the current authoritative-state conflict: old culling plan versus vNext direction; stale `NEXT_STEPS`; old `docs/PROGRESS`; ROADMAP status-vocabulary drift.
89	- Record one explicit decision superseding the fixed three-lane cap with policy-derived capacity. Preserve three as an optional conservative default only if the owner wants it.
90	- Record that vNext amends the current canon in place and that this external roadmap has no normative authority.
91	- Capture the current mandatory-load manifest, installed/source divergence, CI state and task/gate timing baseline before another structural change.
92	
93	Exit: canonical sources and their roles are named; no implementation starts from stale status.
94	
95	### R0.5 — legacy-host census and migration contract
96	
97	- Extend the existing catch-up/adoption contract with owner-authorized discovery, legacy-shape detection, dry run, field-level old-to-new mapping, checkpoint, interruption/resume, rollback and a readable before/after report.
98	- Cover missing/corrupt metadata, custom filenames, profiles and onboarding answers, queue/work graph, decisions/provenance, hooks/gates, installed and external skills, local state and paired repositories.
99	- Define supported versions, mixed-version behavior, shared-machine state, the shadow coexistence window and one-writer ownership during cutover.
100	- Build historical fixture hosts and select three real rehearsals: oldest available host, paired/multi-repository host and customized-profile host.
101	
102	Exit: an unchanged legacy LiveSpec remains the safe fallback; no host is converted before the migrator/validator proves dry-run, idempotence, resume and rollback.
103	
104	### R1 — parity and documentation consolidation
105	
106	- Build the two ledgers from existing requirements, roadmap/decision entries, architecture nodes, tests and operational scripts.
107	- Group the 245 live queue rows under the seven capability groups without deleting their individual acceptance conditions.
108	- Identify exact golden journeys and current proofs.
109	- Catalogue every canonical document by audience, purpose, owned facts, excluded content, load tier, links, archive rule and migration rule.
110	- Resolve competing status/history surfaces and define cross-document contradiction and duplication checks.
111	
112	Exit: 100% of current capabilities/mechanisms and canonical facts have a migration status and owner; unmapped means blocked.
113	
114	### R2 — shadow thin router and minimal loader
115	
116	- Implement a read-only router that produces a decision trace but changes no state.
117	- First two journeys: one real local change and one real cross-cutting software feature.
118	- Old LiveSpec remains the executor; compare route, files read, agents/worktrees, tests, approvals and fallback.
119	- Load only compact confirmed selectors and the router at startup. Route policies and craft skills load by an explicit trigger.
120	- Record shadow output outside canonical task state until its route takes ownership.
121	
122	Exit: router is equal or more conservative on risk, materially lowers mandatory context and never creates a new authoritative task store.
123	
124	### R2.5 — logical skill decoupling
125	
126	- Give every skill a stable trigger, input, output, dependency, owner, failure mode, compatibility range and proof.
127	- Remove the obligation for every selected skill to load the entire base; preserve a legacy adapter fallback.
128	- Keep canonical skill sources in the pack during this phase. Measure real route loads before choosing physical repository boundaries.
129	
130	Exit: each shadow route loads only its required modules and the old monolithic path remains selectable.
131	
132	### R3 — adaptive onboarding and project selection
133	
134	- Separate compact user execution preferences from project kind/layers/proofs.
135	- Make budget/capacity, autonomy, approval and communication settings explicit inputs to the scheduler.
136	- Replace the blocking seven-question setup with progressive discovery: inspect named/project sources first, start safe useful work, and ask one high-value question only when an answer changes the route.
137	- Keep observations session-local. Persist direct user statements and individually confirmed proposals; label source, date and status; support inspect, correct, revoke and delete.
138	- Define privacy, redaction and retention for chat-derived task/profile state. Autonomy, spending, external sharing and durable retention never increase by inference.
139	
140	Exit: new, existing and legacy projects complete their onboarding journeys; the same task produces explainably different policies for different confirmed preferences without changing correctness guarantees.
141	
142	### R4 — calibrated estimates and execution scheduler in shadow mode
143	
144	- Extend the existing work-board estimate/actual contract with task-type, reach, route and project-class evidence; report a range, confidence and comparable-sample count.
145	- Use conservative priors when history is sparse, separate active machine time from waiting/human time, freeze the estimate at take-up and record overrun causes without revising the promise retroactively.
146	- Compute independence from reach/write set, dependencies and shared resources.
147	- Choose dynamic agent count/model/worktrees; allow 20 independent worktrees when capacity and isolation permit.
148	- Optimize for useful completion time and budget rather than maximum concurrency; preserve one-pen integration, ownership, conflict/fallback, recovery, cancellation and fairness across projects.
149	
150	Exit: golden journeys cover calibrated/uncertain estimates, independent parallel work, conflicting writes, shared resources, dead agent, stale worktree, cross-project fairness and unsure classification.
151	
152	### R5 — route-by-route activation
153	
154	- Activate local change and local bug first: focused proofs, no plan/journal/fresh reviewer by default.
155	- Then activate cross-cutting software feature with complete spec/prover/architecture/matrix/test machinery.
156	- Then decision, debt, documentation/publish, feedback and project-kind-specific routes.
157	- Each route retains a one-switch fallback to the old pipeline.
158	
159	Exit: each activated route passes product and operational parity gates.
160	
161	### R6 — work graph and readable board
162	
163	- Implement the already specified work-board capability rather than introducing `cards.yaml` or a third feature list.
164	- Preserve backlog → inception → ready → in-work → done, relation/dependency graph, task updates during execution, on-demand history, branch/worktree/worker details and readable frozen task names.
165	- Derive the board from canonical queue/evidence; load it only for intake/ownership/status work.
166	
167	Exit: every spoken work item is findable and correctly related; the board is readable without loading its full history into execution sessions.
168	
169	### R7 — publish and physically extract proven skill modules
170	
171	- Apply the proven product-prover pattern: thin pack adapter → external/canonical module → phase-specific references with exact triggers.
172	- Extract `text-audit` as a portable document-quality core plus an optional LiveSpec adapter after its documentation contract is stable; then independent review/audit skills; communication/feedback after profile contracts; spec-author/test-author/build-pipeline only after route contracts stabilize.
173	- Pin immutable external revisions, declare compatibility ranges, verify integrity and retain offline/last-known-good rollback.
174	- Split base and remaining skills according to observed routes, not arbitrary byte targets.
175	- Convert global per-turn hooks into policy/event modules where operational parity allows it.
176	
177	Exit: startup and task-specific context fall without weakening route proofs or fallbacks.
178	
179	### R8 — migrate hosts, cut over routes and retire old control prose
180	
181	- Cut over one route at a time after shadow agreement and golden journeys.
182	- Rehearse and then migrate legacy hosts through the accepted R0.5 contract; mixed old/new hosts remain supported for the declared window.
183	- Archive or remove old control prose only when its ledger entries are retained or explicitly deprecated.
184	- Keep specs/tests as durable oracle; retire campaign/status duplication.
185	
186	Exit: 100% critical journeys green, zero lost tested claims, improved context/approval/agent/test metrics, explicit owner acceptance.
187	
188	## Golden journeys
189	
190	1. Answer-only chat message creates no work artifact.
191	2. Local one-owner change uses focused proof and no fresh reviewer.
192	3. Local bug receives regression test and class sweep.
193	4. Cross-cutting software feature follows spec → proofs → architecture → matrix → tests → code.
194	5. Documentation-only change uses prose route.
195	6. Decision records one durable owner ruling and updates affected contract.
196	7. Debt is parked with a revisit trigger and no execution.
197	8. Project kind selects different layers/proofs.
198	9. Twenty independent work items can use isolated worktrees under sufficient capacity.
199	10. Conflicting reach/write sets serialize under one pen.
200	11. Shared test/resource contention limits concurrency without a fixed global cap.
201	12. Unsure classification takes the conservative old/full route.
202	13. An agent dies or loses its worktree; state and ownership recover.
203	14. Installed skill is stale; sync/install route blocks or repairs explicitly.
204	15. Push/release lacks proof; fallback blocks without creating a review storm.
205	16. A task receives new user words while running; the same item absorbs them and preserves on-demand history.
206	17. A first conversation begins useful safe work and asks only the first consequential unknown.
207	18. Repository evidence produces a clearly labelled proposal; it changes durable policy only after acceptance.
208	19. A person changes or revokes communication, pace, budget or autonomy settings and the next route reflects it.
209	20. A private chat fragment becomes at most a redacted summary under the chosen retention policy.
210	21. Russian chat produces native, readable English canonical documents.
211	22. A common task class receives an evidence-backed time range; a novel class receives a low-confidence conservative range.
212	23. Estimated, active, waiting and end-to-end time settle separately at close and recalibrate later estimates.
213	24. An old host dry-runs, migrates, resumes after interruption and rolls back without losing facts.
214	25. Old and vNext sessions coexist in shadow mode without writing the same canonical state.
215	
216	## Measurement
217	
218	- startup context bytes/files;
219	- task context bytes/files before first action;
220	- time to first useful action;
221	- human approvals/interventions per completed item;
222	- agents/worktrees and redundant reviews per item;
223	- focused/full test runs and total machine time;
224	- management prose bytes per functional change;
225	- router-versus-old-route disagreements;
226	- mapped capabilities/mechanisms and lost tested claims.
227	- estimate calibration error and interval coverage by task class/reach/route/project;
228	- active, machine, waiting and end-to-end time kept distinct;
229	- onboarding questions before first useful action, inferred proposals accepted/rejected, preference corrections/revocations;
230	- legacy hosts discovered, dry-run, migrated, resumed and rolled back successfully.
231	
232	The baseline begins with shadow journeys, not the recent emergency migration commits.
233	
234	## Canonical document update bundles
235	
236	| Change kind | Documents that move together |
237	|---|---|
238	| Product capability or user-visible route | `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` → `ARCHITECTURE.md` → `TEST_MATRIX.md` → tests → `ROADMAP.md` status |
239	| Operational mechanism with unchanged product promise | `ARCHITECTURE.md` → `TEST_MATRIX.md`/guardrail tests → implementation; product spec only if the guarantee changes |
240	| Work board surface | `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` + `ARCHITECTURE.md` + `SURFACES.md` + `TEST_MATRIX.md` + board tests + accepted norm |
241	| Profile/onboarding behavior | `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` + `ARCHITECTURE.md` + adoption/templates/profile schema + `TEST_MATRIX.md` + tests |
242	| Estimate/calibration behavior | existing work-board clauses in `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` + work-board/scheduler nodes in `ARCHITECTURE.md` + existing estimate/actual matrix rows + calibration tests |
243	| Legacy-host migration | existing migration/adoption requirements + `MIGRATION.md` + `ARCHITECTURE.md` migration seams + `TEST_MATRIX.md` + historical fixture-host tests |
244	| Documentation information architecture | existing document/surface requirements + `ARCHITECTURE.md` ownership/seams + `SURFACES.md` + contradiction/duplication/load-tier tests |
245	| Skill logical decoupling/extraction | `ARCHITECTURE.md` + adapter/install/release contracts + compatibility/bare-checkout/offline/rollback tests; product spec only for changed user-visible guarantees |
246	| Local implementation preserving contract | implementation + focused test + commit; no plan/journal/review prose by default |
247	| Explicit deprecation | `DECISIONS.md` owner ruling + parity ledger + affected canonical documents/tests in the same migration |
248	
249	`README.md` and `OVERVIEW.md` update after a vertical slice proves the reader-facing claim, not before.
250	
251	## First vertical slice
252	
253	Shadow-route one real local change and one cross-cutting software feature. The router emits only:
254	
255	`task type · reach/risk · selected route · owner · agents/worktrees · required proof · fallback · sources used`
256	
257	The old pipeline executes both. Compare decisions and measured cost. No board implementation, new task database, personas, always-loaded rulebook or cutover occurs in this slice.

- a work board with backlog/inception/ready/in-work/done, readable cards, task history, lanes, worktrees, estimates and actuals;
- personal and host profiles, project kinds, layers, proof kinds, onboarding and adoption;
- alternate routes for feature, bug, refactor, documentation and feedback;
- spec → prover → architecture → prover → matrix → tests → code traceability;
- agent cards, zones, ownership, dependency graph, isolated worktrees and one-pen integration;
- gates, fallback, install/sync, recovery, release and push controls.

The defect is composition: these capabilities are fused into a 64 KB always-read base skill, other large skills, global hooks, and several competing status/history surfaces. vNext should replace the always-on control layer, not discard the capabilities or their machinery.

## Target architecture

1. **Thin router — always loaded.** Reads only the minimum user/project selectors, classifies answer versus work, determines task type and reach, and returns route, owner, execution policy, required proof and fallback.
2. **User policy — on demand.** Budget/capacity, autonomy, approval thresholds, communication preferences and reporting density.
3. **Project policy — on demand.** Project kind, stack, layers, proof kinds, sources of truth, install/release policy and available routes.
4. **Route catalogue — on demand.** Local change, local bug, cross-cutting feature, decision, debt, documentation/publish, feedback and project-kind-specific quality routes.
5. **Execution scheduler — on demand.** Computes agent count and model tier from budget, independent reach/write sets, worktrees, dependencies and shared resources. No permanent three-agent ceiling. One-pen and conflict guarantees remain.
6. **Evidence layer.** Existing specs, architecture, matrix, tests, prover records and commits remain the sources of contract and proof. Task state points to them and never restates them.
7. **Human visibility.** The existing work-board capability is implemented as a readable, derived/on-demand view over the canonical queue and evidence. It is not a new competing feature list or an always-read session document.
8. **Adaptive relationship policy — on demand.** Existing founding, adoption, profiles and the settings card become a progressive learning loop. Session observations remain ephemeral; only the person's words or individually accepted proposals become durable settings. The system starts useful work immediately and asks when uncertainty changes safety, cost or outcome.
9. **Estimator and calibration — on demand.** The existing work-board estimate/actual contract learns distributions by task type, reach, route and project. It returns a range and confidence with its evidence, freezes the estimate at take-up, records actual and end-to-end time at close, and recalibrates without rewriting history.

## Capability groups

| Group | Existing material to retain | vNext change |
|---|---|---|
| Intake and durable routing | wish/feedback intake, queue, inbox, decisions | thin pre-rulebook router; answer/no-work exit; one home per work item |
| Work graph and board | ROADMAP row 166/566, Requirement 309, work-board architecture target | readable derived board; inception; dependencies; collapsible details/history; no third feature map |
| Profiles and onboarding | settings ladder, personal/host profiles, project.kind/layers/proofs, founding/adoption, settings card | progressive discovery; observed/inferred/confirmed/revoked distinction; compact confirmed selectors; privacy and retention; adapt only inside consented bounds |
| Route catalogue | existing nine-station software pipeline and bug/refactor/docs shortcuts | executable/selectable route map rather than duplicated prose |
| Scheduler, estimates and agents | dependency graph, zones, agent cards, worktrees, lane opening, one pen, work-board estimate/actual fields | calibrated ranges by task class/reach/route/project; dynamic capacity by budget/reach/resources; model/skill assignment; shared-resource reservations |
| Traceability and quality | spec/architecture/matrix/test mappings, prover, design/text passes | preserve as compatibility oracle; load only the proof module required by the route |
| Lifecycle operations | gates, fallback, install/sync, CI, push, release, recovery | explicit route riders and conservative fallback; no universal review/full-suite ceremony |

Later selectable product-quality modules remain in scope: feature-fit, visitor/feel validation, default expiry, consequence-first decisions, feedback measurement/A-B and project-kind-specific design/proof passes.

## Compatibility ledgers required before cutover

### Product parity

`old capability → canonical source → vNext module/route → proof → retained | deferred | deprecated`

### Operational parity

`old mechanism → trigger → required state → owner → execution → verification → failure fallback → vNext equivalent → proof → retained | deferred | deprecated`

No capability or mechanism is removed as a duplicate. `deprecated` requires an explicit owner decision. `deferred` continues to use the old LiveSpec route.

The ledgers record proof state as `specified → implemented → tested → installed → invoked → evidence current`. A green string test does not prove an exercised mechanism.

## Canonical-amendment rule

There will be no parallel vNext product specification. This roadmap is an external migration worksheet only. Accepted behavior is amended in the existing canonical homes:

- adaptive onboarding extends the existing founding, personal-profile, project-kind and settings-card requirements and their current architecture nodes;
- estimates extend the existing work-board statement, estimate/actual and delivery-trail clauses rather than creating an estimator specification beside them;
- work-graph schema and history extend the existing work-board requirement and node;
- legacy-host conversion extends the existing catch-up/adoption/migration requirements and `MIGRATION.md`;
- routing extends the existing door, kind, footprint and reach contracts;
- documentation structure belongs in the existing document/surface contracts;
- skill extraction is an architecture/install/release change and changes the product spec only where user-visible guarantees change.

Every accepted change lands as one coordinated delta: product promise first, then architecture owner/seams, matrix proof, red-first tests, implementation and ROADMAP status. Existing anchors are retained or explicitly migrated; they are not copied into a second namespace.

## Prioritized roadmap

### R0 — stop drift and establish the migration baseline

- Freeze new pruning, skill extraction and guardrail growth except blockers for the migration itself.
- Preserve the six current commits and the three protected dirty documents.
- Resolve the current authoritative-state conflict: old culling plan versus vNext direction; stale `NEXT_STEPS`; old `docs/PROGRESS`; ROADMAP status-vocabulary drift.
- Record one explicit decision superseding the fixed three-lane cap with policy-derived capacity. Preserve three as an optional conservative default only if the owner wants it.
- Record that vNext amends the current canon in place and that this external roadmap has no normative authority.
- Capture the current mandatory-load manifest, installed/source divergence, CI state and task/gate timing baseline before another structural change.

Exit: canonical sources and their roles are named; no implementation starts from stale status.

### R0.5 — legacy-host census and migration contract

- Extend the existing catch-up/adoption contract with owner-authorized discovery, legacy-shape detection, dry run, field-level old-to-new mapping, checkpoint, interruption/resume, rollback and a readable before/after report.
- Cover missing/corrupt metadata, custom filenames, profiles and onboarding answers, queue/work graph, decisions/provenance, hooks/gates, installed and external skills, local state and paired repositories.
- Define supported versions, mixed-version behavior, shared-machine state, the shadow coexistence window and one-writer ownership during cutover.
- Build historical fixture hosts and select three real rehearsals: oldest available host, paired/multi-repository host and customized-profile host.

Exit: an unchanged legacy LiveSpec remains the safe fallback; no host is converted before the migrator/validator proves dry-run, idempotence, resume and rollback.

### R1 — parity and documentation consolidation

- Build the two ledgers from existing requirements, roadmap/decision entries, architecture nodes, tests and operational scripts.
- Group the 245 live queue rows under the seven capability groups without deleting their individual acceptance conditions.
- Identify exact golden journeys and current proofs.
- Catalogue every canonical document by audience, purpose, owned facts, excluded content, load tier, links, archive rule and migration rule.
- Resolve competing status/history surfaces and define cross-document contradiction and duplication checks.

Exit: 100% of current capabilities/mechanisms and canonical facts have a migration status and owner; unmapped means blocked.

### R2 — shadow thin router and minimal loader

- Implement a read-only router that produces a decision trace but changes no state.
- First two journeys: one real local change and one real cross-cutting software feature.
- Old LiveSpec remains the executor; compare route, files read, agents/worktrees, tests, approvals and fallback.
- Load only compact confirmed selectors and the router at startup. Route policies and craft skills load by an explicit trigger.
- Record shadow output outside canonical task state until its route takes ownership.

Exit: router is equal or more conservative on risk, materially lowers mandatory context and never creates a new authoritative task store.

### R2.5 — logical skill decoupling

- Give every skill a stable trigger, input, output, dependency, owner, failure mode, compatibility range and proof.
- Remove the obligation for every selected skill to load the entire base; preserve a legacy adapter fallback.
- Keep canonical skill sources in the pack during this phase. Measure real route loads before choosing physical repository boundaries.

Exit: each shadow route loads only its required modules and the old monolithic path remains selectable.

### R3 — adaptive onboarding and project selection

- Separate compact user execution preferences from project kind/layers/proofs.
- Make budget/capacity, autonomy, approval and communication settings explicit inputs to the scheduler.
- Replace the blocking seven-question setup with progressive discovery: inspect named/project sources first, start safe useful work, and ask one high-value question only when an answer changes the route.
- Keep observations session-local. Persist direct user statements and individually confirmed proposals; label source, date and status; support inspect, correct, revoke and delete.
- Define privacy, redaction and retention for chat-derived task/profile state. Autonomy, spending, external sharing and durable retention never increase by inference.

Exit: new, existing and legacy projects complete their onboarding journeys; the same task produces explainably different policies for different confirmed preferences without changing correctness guarantees.

### R4 — calibrated estimates and execution scheduler in shadow mode

- Extend the existing work-board estimate/actual contract with task-type, reach, route and project-class evidence; report a range, confidence and comparable-sample count.
- Use conservative priors when history is sparse, separate active machine time from waiting/human time, freeze the estimate at take-up and record overrun causes without revising the promise retroactively.
- Compute independence from reach/write set, dependencies and shared resources.
- Choose dynamic agent count/model/worktrees; allow 20 independent worktrees when capacity and isolation permit.
- Optimize for useful completion time and budget rather than maximum concurrency; preserve one-pen integration, ownership, conflict/fallback, recovery, cancellation and fairness across projects.

Exit: golden journeys cover calibrated/uncertain estimates, independent parallel work, conflicting writes, shared resources, dead agent, stale worktree, cross-project fairness and unsure classification.

### R5 — route-by-route activation

- Activate local change and local bug first: focused proofs, no plan/journal/fresh reviewer by default.
- Then activate cross-cutting software feature with complete spec/prover/architecture/matrix/test machinery.
- Then decision, debt, documentation/publish, feedback and project-kind-specific routes.
- Each route retains a one-switch fallback to the old pipeline.

Exit: each activated route passes product and operational parity gates.

### R6 — work graph and readable board

- Implement the already specified work-board capability rather than introducing `cards.yaml` or a third feature list.
- Preserve backlog → inception → ready → in-work → done, relation/dependency graph, task updates during execution, on-demand history, branch/worktree/worker details and readable frozen task names.
- Derive the board from canonical queue/evidence; load it only for intake/ownership/status work.

Exit: every spoken work item is findable and correctly related; the board is readable without loading its full history into execution sessions.

### R7 — publish and physically extract proven skill modules

- Apply the proven product-prover pattern: thin pack adapter → external/canonical module → phase-specific references with exact triggers.
- Extract `text-audit` as a portable document-quality core plus an optional LiveSpec adapter after its documentation contract is stable; then independent review/audit skills; communication/feedback after profile contracts; spec-author/test-author/build-pipeline only after route contracts stabilize.
- Pin immutable external revisions, declare compatibility ranges, verify integrity and retain offline/last-known-good rollback.
- Split base and remaining skills according to observed routes, not arbitrary byte targets.
- Convert global per-turn hooks into policy/event modules where operational parity allows it.

Exit: startup and task-specific context fall without weakening route proofs or fallbacks.

### R8 — migrate hosts, cut over routes and retire old control prose

- Cut over one route at a time after shadow agreement and golden journeys.
- Rehearse and then migrate legacy hosts through the accepted R0.5 contract; mixed old/new hosts remain supported for the declared window.
- Archive or remove old control prose only when its ledger entries are retained or explicitly deprecated.
- Keep specs/tests as durable oracle; retire campaign/status duplication.

Exit: 100% critical journeys green, zero lost tested claims, improved context/approval/agent/test metrics, explicit owner acceptance.

## Golden journeys

1. Answer-only chat message creates no work artifact.
2. Local one-owner change uses focused proof and no fresh reviewer.
3. Local bug receives regression test and class sweep.
4. Cross-cutting software feature follows spec → proofs → architecture → matrix → tests → code.
5. Documentation-only change uses prose route.
6. Decision records one durable owner ruling and updates affected contract.
7. Debt is parked with a revisit trigger and no execution.
8. Project kind selects different layers/proofs.
9. Twenty independent work items can use isolated worktrees under sufficient capacity.
10. Conflicting reach/write sets serialize under one pen.
11. Shared test/resource contention limits concurrency without a fixed global cap.
12. Unsure classification takes the conservative old/full route.
13. An agent dies or loses its worktree; state and ownership recover.
14. Installed skill is stale; sync/install route blocks or repairs explicitly.
15. Push/release lacks proof; fallback blocks without creating a review storm.
16. A task receives new user words while running; the same item absorbs them and preserves on-demand history.
17. A first conversation begins useful safe work and asks only the first consequential unknown.
18. Repository evidence produces a clearly labelled proposal; it changes durable policy only after acceptance.
19. A person changes or revokes communication, pace, budget or autonomy settings and the next route reflects it.
20. A private chat fragment becomes at most a redacted summary under the chosen retention policy.
21. Russian chat produces native, readable English canonical documents.
22. A common task class receives an evidence-backed time range; a novel class receives a low-confidence conservative range.
23. Estimated, active, waiting and end-to-end time settle separately at close and recalibrate later estimates.
24. An old host dry-runs, migrates, resumes after interruption and rolls back without losing facts.
25. Old and vNext sessions coexist in shadow mode without writing the same canonical state.

## Measurement

- startup context bytes/files;
- task context bytes/files before first action;
- time to first useful action;
- human approvals/interventions per completed item;
- agents/worktrees and redundant reviews per item;
- focused/full test runs and total machine time;
- management prose bytes per functional change;
- router-versus-old-route disagreements;
- mapped capabilities/mechanisms and lost tested claims.
- estimate calibration error and interval coverage by task class/reach/route/project;
- active, machine, waiting and end-to-end time kept distinct;
- onboarding questions before first useful action, inferred proposals accepted/rejected, preference corrections/revocations;
- legacy hosts discovered, dry-run, migrated, resumed and rolled back successfully.

The baseline begins with shadow journeys, not the recent emergency migration commits.

## Canonical document update bundles

| Change kind | Documents that move together |
|---|---|
| Product capability or user-visible route | `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` → `ARCHITECTURE.md` → `TEST_MATRIX.md` → tests → `ROADMAP.md` status |
| Operational mechanism with unchanged product promise | `ARCHITECTURE.md` → `TEST_MATRIX.md`/guardrail tests → implementation; product spec only if the guarantee changes |
| Work board surface | `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` + `ARCHITECTURE.md` + `SURFACES.md` + `TEST_MATRIX.md` + board tests + accepted norm |
| Profile/onboarding behavior | `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` + `ARCHITECTURE.md` + adoption/templates/profile schema + `TEST_MATRIX.md` + tests |
| Estimate/calibration behavior | existing work-board clauses in `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` + work-board/scheduler nodes in `ARCHITECTURE.md` + existing estimate/actual matrix rows + calibration tests |
| Legacy-host migration | existing migration/adoption requirements + `MIGRATION.md` + `ARCHITECTURE.md` migration seams + `TEST_MATRIX.md` + historical fixture-host tests |
| Documentation information architecture | existing document/surface requirements + `ARCHITECTURE.md` ownership/seams + `SURFACES.md` + contradiction/duplication/load-tier tests |
| Skill logical decoupling/extraction | `ARCHITECTURE.md` + adapter/install/release contracts + compatibility/bare-checkout/offline/rollback tests; product spec only for changed user-visible guarantees |
| Local implementation preserving contract | implementation + focused test + commit; no plan/journal/review prose by default |
| Explicit deprecation | `DECISIONS.md` owner ruling + parity ledger + affected canonical documents/tests in the same migration |

`README.md` and `OVERVIEW.md` update after a vertical slice proves the reader-facing claim, not before.

## First vertical slice

Shadow-route one real local change and one cross-cutting software feature. The router emits only:

`task type · reach/risk · selected route · owner · agents/worktrees · required proof · fallback · sources used`

The old pipeline executes both. Compare decisions and measured cost. No board implementation, new task database, personas, always-loaded rulebook or cutover occurs in this slice.

All from `/Users/sashaabramovich/live-spec/PRODUCT_SPEC.md` (8225 lines, v4.3.0). Requirement headings are the anchors (`## Requirement N: <title>`; GitHub-style slug from the full heading text).

## The nine requirements

**Req 23 — L757 — "Every ask hears its price in time, and the landing settles it"** (invariants INV-93/27/35). Topic: estimates and actuals. Four criteria (L767-771): capture echo carries "an honest time range read from the work's known shape or observed runs, stating an unknown as unknown"; work ≥ one hour is "explain[ed] up front in plain steps — what has to happen and why it takes that long" plus remaining time on the heartbeat; at landing "state the estimate beside the actual in the delivery report, saying an overrun or an under plainly"; a direct command holding the session "more than a beat" also hears its range even though it registers no row. Carries an open `[GAP]` at L772: the beat's duration for a direct command is unstated.

**Req 170 — L3908 — "Founding asks its shaping questions and never infers them"** (B-2). Topic: onboarding/founding. Founding must answer the founding questions in the new spec's opening before working the first request; the personal-tool-vs-reusable-product question comes first and is the one open question that *blocks* the first request ("an ordinary open question rides along without stopping work, and this one *shall* not", L3920). Answer comes from the personal profile's personal-scope standing preference (seeded and said aloud) or from asking the human; "*shall* derive no founding answer from example artifacts ... an inferred founding answer is a silent micro-decision at its most expensive" (L3926). Adoption's orient re-puts the same questions (L3930).

**Req 171 — L3934 — "Founding learns who the human is"** (B-3, E-13). Topic: personal profile. Look for the personal profile "at its one home" at founding, at adoption's orient, and at first session on a new machine or with a new human; if present, load it, name the file, and "read any unrecognized line aloud instead of skipping it silently"; if absent, offer creation from `templates/profile.template.md`. Human-told lines written faithfully; named sources (repos, docs, public page) are read and proposed line by line, accepted or dropped on the human's word, "A dropped proposal *shall* stay dropped." Template marks every placeholder so nothing passes for the human's word. Declining runs the session on pack defaults, said aloud, re-offered at next project setup rather than mid-work; existing profile skips the step; "A worker session *shall* onboard no one; its brief already carries the setting lines it needs" (L3958).

**Req 180 — L4172 — "The catch-up sequence brings an adopted host onto the current pack" [feature: F-catchup]** (A-11, INV-91). Topic: migration/catch-up. A pack release that owes host action lands "one dated, versioned migration chapter"; a release owing nothing adds none and says so in its changelog. Work list = ordered chain of chapters from the host's recorded pack version to current, oldest first; unreadable version starts at the earliest chapter. Four fixed phases: "orient on the delta, plan behind the owner's gate, execute while preserving facts, then verify and re-record" (L4183). Orient reads installed-set record + tree + pack journal; "*when* preconditions in the guide disagree with the tree, the system *shall* take the tree as the truth". Never-answered founding questions are named by reading the host's `founding.set-version` (INV-227). Plan lives in `.live-spec/adopt/`, lists every file that moves/merges/retires and every conflict, and "*shall* move no file before the owner's word". Execute opens with a clean-tree baseline commit under checkpoint discipline and resumes from checkpoint. Verify runs the host's gates and suite, re-records the installed-set record, lands one journal chapter. Machine-shared steps (installed-skills folder, personal profile) run once per machine with an already-done check.

**Req 181 — L4201 — "Every catch-up step is safe on a half-done state"** (INV-89/90, E-16). Topic: idempotent migration + fact preservation. Each step reads its precondition from the tree; an already-held end state is reported done and skipped; old-and-new both present merges file by file; identical content drops the old copy to the attic. Differing profile files reconcile by the settings ladder (host-profile line whose home is the personal profile moves up; host-scoped stays), and a line moving into a machine-shared file follows "the promotion law and re-read that file immediately before appending". Other conflicts ride the plan to the owner's gate; "*shall* never nest a directory inside its replacement and *shall* never overwrite the new form with the old". Settled prose rewritten only on owner rejection or when the new shape cannot hold it, each rewrite carried on the plan. Host-chosen document names are kept and recorded as host-profile lines (`spec.file: SPEC.md`). Outdated installed-set records (e.g. commit pins) retire to the attic; "The skills on disk *shall* be the authoritative set." Stray state files re-homed (root checkpoint → `.live-spec/checkpoints/`, closed → attic, look-alike dir merged).

**Req 182 — L4231 — "Catch-up proves itself and stays restorable"** (INV-92, A-5). Topic: migration provenance/verification. Pre-sequence inventory beside the plan: "every document with a content fingerprint, the host spec's anchor multiset, and the suite's verdict and count as found"; same inventory after execute, then compared. "Every difference *shall* be accounted for by a plan item — a file unchanged, re-homed to a named path, merged from named sources, or resting in the attic under its manifest line; an anchor delta *shall* match a change the plan names; and the suite *shall* read at least as green as before" (L4243). An unaccounted difference blocks verify until the owner amends the plan or the step is reverted. Restore point: the plan names the baseline commit and "the one command that returns the host to the pre-sequence state"; the attic keeps every superseded file readable without any restore. Documents-and-records-only sequences skip the facet sweep.

**Req 186 — L4324 — "The settings card shows at setup and answers the standing question" [feature: F-onboarding]** (INV-87/88). Topic: settings card / customization surface — your guess was right. Rendered at end of founding and at end of adoption's orient once project kind and economy setting settle. Every setting the pack knows gets a row: plain-words name, current value for this host, one line on how to change it in plain speech; "A recorded default *shall* be shown as told, and the card *shall* ask nothing." Values read from the settings ladder (reader's profiles + host's recorded lines); opened by the show rule after the pre-show register lint. The same card, re-rendered from current truth, answers "what can I customize" in any wording, "and *shall* let no hand-kept copy answer." One catalog home: pack-defaults table joined with profile files and host lines; "No second hand-kept settings list *shall* exist", with bidirectional traceability (missing card-visible row and sourceless card row are each a defect). Copy states rules; a personal value (a language, a name) shows only as the reader's current value, "The fixed copy *shall* never present one person's value as the product's prescription." Rendered by `scripts/onboarding-card.py`, failing loudly on a malformed table row; missing profile renders pack defaults and names the founding offer; new table rows get card rule-copy drafted on the clean-writer road. Facets: single-column on phone/narrow, static plain HTML with headings and keyboard scrolling, no hover; empty = missing profile, error = malformed catalog row, blocked = flagged text at register lint; rendering is read-only and concurrent, an open card shows its render moment and does not live-update.

**Req 274 — L6581 — "A release's number reports what taking it costs a host"** (INV-217, INV-91). Topic: semantic versioning defined by host-side cost — not package docs. Patch = a machine fixed to hold an already-stated law, no new capability or changed contract, "which the host takes by doing nothing". Minor = backward-compatible growth (new capability, law, gate), "which the host takes by re-running its catch-up walk with nothing it already carries rewritten". Major = cannot be taken without the host changing what it carries, and ships a dated migration chapter (reworded vendored rule, renamed/removed surface, changed adoption or catch-up step, moved law forcing host action). Default is patch, raised only where earned; the minor-vs-major call is "a stated guidance the releasing session applies and names, held by no gate, the same standing as a design-review finding that never blocks a lane". Homed in the base rulebook, build-pipeline's commit-and-show step, and here.

**Req 309 — L7620 — "The work board shows the whole queue in columns — the work in hand, the work done, and what each took" [feature: F-work-board]**, marked `[target]` (nothing built yet), invariants INV-308 through INV-313, 99 criteria (L7634-7783). Topic: the work-board surface, statements/estimates/actuals.
- Preserves: departures board, narration, "the capture echo's honest range and the delivery report's estimate beside actual as they stand" (L7637), routine/status reports, chat live status line.
- Identity: the rendered status page grown up; one source file per host; published at one stable link; registered in `SURFACES.md` with marker text and spec anchors before it renders; leads with the one-line identifier; passes the concurrent-edit fence with blocked-write re-read-and-reapply.

No inferred line shall raise autonomy, spending, external sharing, retention or a safety threshold. A chat fragment persists at most as a redacted summary under the recorded retention setting. Lines recorded before this law keep their standing unchanged." **Архитектура:** расширение host-contract (схема строки профиля: source/date/status); шов :636 без изменений. **Матрица:** расширить блок M-051/M-206–M-213; новые строки inspect/correct/revoke. **Миграция:** minor; глава catch-up лишь помечает старые строки «recorded before source-labelling», не переписывая (Req 181, запрет blanket-rewrite). **Зависимость:** после 1.

The push check reads the same vocabulary from the landed diff. When the two disagree, or either is unsure, the conservative fuller route holds and both readings are recorded. **Дома:** Req 309 (99 критериев), узел work-board, M-519–M-544 (все todo), строки 166/566, кластер DECISIONS :105–184. **Сохраняется:** всё специфицированное: одна исходная папка-файл, фриз формулировок, производность от queue/архива (швы :660–665), «board никогда не пишет историю журнала». **Разрыв:** словарь колонок vs inception (см. вердикт); честная оговорка ARCHITECTURE:696 — coverage-строка закрыта соседним тестом; статус «ready» ни разу не породжён. **Норма (EN):** одно сверочное предложение в Req 309: "The column set reads backlog (awaiting validation), inception, ready, in work, done, matching the recorded stage-ladder ruling; each column states its one leaving condition." **Архитектура:** без новых узлов; регистрация в `SURFACES.md` до рендера (M-521). **Матрица:** блок M-519–M-544 переходит из todo в built; M-544 остаётся человеко-проверяемым с флагом. **Миграция:** minor. **Зависимость:** после 4 (поля оценок в statement).

**Дома:** Req 180–182, Req 274, `MIGRATION.md`, узел attach, M-217–M-221/248/249/327/332/336. **Сохраняется:** четыре фазы, half-done-law, чекпоинт-резюме, baseline-commit + одна команда восстановления, цепочка глав, INV-10 «один писатель». **Разрыв:** dry-run отсутствует (ноль вхождений); смешанные версии описаны только для пар; skills, установленные не паком, не упомянуты вовсе; тесты проверяют прозу, а не прогон; долг строки 602 (глава про rule 30) открыт. **Дома:** строки 618 (references-раскрой product-prover), 458 (text-audit), 619–622; M-327/332/336 (пины sha256, net-parity, оффлайн-класс). **Сохраняется:** прецедент внешнего адаптера product-prover и bare-checkout-контракта; ловушка gate-aa (rule-census в той же посадке). **Разрыв:** порог извлечения не сформулирован как норма. **Норма (EN):** "A skill leaves the pack only after its logical contract stands and its external form proves install from a bare checkout, offline operation on the pinned revision, update by a pin change, and return to the last known-good pin." **Архитектура/матрица:** переиспользовать машинерию vendored-pin; строки по образцу M-327/M-332 на каждый извлечённый модуль. **Миграция:** minor на модуль; глава — только если хост обязан действовать. **Зависимость:** последним, после 3 и 6.

## Inventory — 12 SKILL.md under `skills/` (11 pack + 1 external vendored)

| Skill | v | Trigger (frontmatter) | Base pin | refs/ split |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md`:1-8 | 4.3.0 | "Load before using any live-spec pack skill (…10 named…), before briefing a worker" | n/a (is base) | no |
| `skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md`:1-15 | 4.3.0 | non-trivial feature/bug/refactor/docs-only/removal + setup walks | yes :13 | yes, 8 files |
| `skills/spec-author/SKILL.md`:1-17 | 4.3.0 | start/grow/sync a spec | yes :13 | **no** (746 lines, largest un-split) |
| `skills/product-prover/SKILL.md`:1-11 | 1.3.0 | review/critique/stress-test a doc; "Product Prover" | **no** — explicitly "works on its own" :10 | `reference/` (singular) :11 |
| `skills/product-prover-pack/SKILL.md`:1-13 | 1.0.0 | "whenever product-prover runs inside a live-spec project" | partial (names base :2 refs) | no |
| `skills/design-reviewer/SKILL.md`:1-15 | 4.3.0 | after a spec is proven | yes :11 | **no** (429 lines) |
| `skills/test-author/SKILL.md`:1-15 | 4.3.0 | derive matrix/tests from proven spec | yes :13 | no |
| `skills/communicator/SKILL.md`:1-15 | 4.3.0 | show work / ask a decision | yes :11 | yes, 4 files |
| `skills/feedback-intake/SKILL.md`:1-15 | 4.3.0 | feedback arrives / inbox sweep | yes :13 | no |
| `skills/feedback-collector/SKILL.md`:1-15 | 4.3.0 | "only if enabled" + rare strong reaction | yes :14 | no |
| `skills/text-audit/SKILL.md`:1-15 | 4.3.0 | any human-facing text | yes :11 | yes, 4 files |
| `skills/publish/SKILL.md`:1-15 | 4.3.0 | before work leaves the machine | yes :13 | no |

## Door → skill routing (evidence)

`skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md`:38 defines the closed door set; :107 "name the door aloud" before any tool call; :169 "door set is CLOSED"; table at `references/request-kind-table.md`:6-21.

- **feature** → step 1 `spec-author` (:243) + fit walk + facet sweep (:248-253) → step 2 `product-prover` FULL/CROSS-LINK (:264) → `design-reviewer` on cadence (:275) → steps 5-6 `test-author` → step 9 `publish` shopfront (:667).
- **bug** → matrix step, red-on-bug test (`request-kind-table.md`:10); tripwire at :177; class hunt (:180-188); recurring bug re-doors to feature (:188).
- **refactor** → no spec/matrix delta, enters at step 8 (:196-202); redesign re-routes by INV-113.
- **docs-only** → own light path, no spec/matrix step (:203-204); removal accounting lives in communicator rule 6 (:205); register lint.
- **feedback** → `feedback-intake` (`request-kind-table.md`:18), opens no queue row on its own.
- **setup** (attach/found/catch-up) → `references/project-setup.md` routing card (:217-224), stands outside the derivation chain.

Mode names bind through `skills/product-prover-pack/SKILL.md`:19-23 (`FULL`/`CROSS-LINK`/`FEATURE-FIT`).

## Findings

**1. Roster arity contradiction.** `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md`:8 and :12 and :26 say "ten working skills"; the closing roster :706-708 lists **eleven** (product-prover-pack included). Frontmatter :3 lists only ten and omits product-prover-pack. `build-pipeline`:661 repeats "names the ten working ones". Same drift class as ROADMAP 620.

**2. Version-pin contradiction is live and unrepaired.** `skills/spec-author/SKILL.md`:718-719 forbids "pinning a drifting version number in prose"; `skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md`:477-479 states "no doc pins a drifting version number in prose". Yet ten bodies open on `` `live-spec-base` (v4.3.0) `` — spec-author:13, build-pipeline:13, communicator:11, design-reviewer:11, feedback-collector:14, feedback-intake:13, publish:13, test-author:13, text-audit:11. ROADMAP.md:280 (row 620) has this queued, still `*queued*`.

**3. Prover drift (ROADMAP.md:279, row 619) is now mostly stale as written.** Diff of `editions/product-prover/SKILL.md` vs `skills/product-prover/SKILL.md` is only 14 lines: version `1.2.0-standalone` vs `1.3.0` (:5), mode-name paragraph (:314), the Phase 5 provenance line (skills :712-713), and the live-spec footer. Both now say "Six short blocks" (skills :715, edition :709) and both carry 13 "seam" uses — the row's points 3-5 no longer reproduce. **The edition is the older copy**, so `scripts/sync-mirrors.sh`'s mtime guard (`REFUSAL_STALE`, :122) is the only thing holding them.

**4. No stated trigger / weak trigger.** `product-prover-pack` has no "When it fires" section and no route that names it from build-pipeline's steps (only referenced in the relations list :654) — it is loaded implicitly. `live-spec-base`, `spec-author`, `build-pipeline`, `test-author`, `product-prover` carry no `## When it fires` heading at all; only communicator:24, design-reviewer:89, feedback-collector:40, feedback-intake:29, publish:28, text-audit:108 do.

**5. Circularity.** `design-reviewer` findings re-enter step 2 via spec-author → prover → design-reviewer (`build-pipeline`:275-283) — bounded at three rounds by INV-154, so guarded. Unbounded: `communicator` ↔ `build-pipeline` (build-pipeline:107 requires communicator rule 12; communicator references build-pipeline), and `feedback-intake` ↔ `feedback-collector` (feedback-collector cites feedback-intake 6×). No load-order rule states which opens first.

**6. Whole-base obligation.** `live-spec-base` is 708 lines and its frontmatter says "Load before using any live-spec pack skill" with no section-level entry points — every skill's opener pins it whole. Ten skills therefore carry a full-base load cost for what is usually two or three `base rule N` references.

## Eight-field logical contract — per-skill coverage

| Field | Present | Absent |
|---|---|---|
| **trigger** | 12/12 in frontmatter description; 6/12 also as a body section | — |
| **inputs** | implicit only (prose "Where the paths point"); explicit nowhere | **absent across the board** |
| **outputs** | named as record paths: design-reviewer:374 (`docs/design-review/`), build-pipeline:264 (`docs/prover/`), feedback-collector:112 (`outbox/`), product-prover-pack:40, spec-author:701 ("What spec-author produces") | communicator, publish, test-author, text-audit, live-spec-base state none |
| **dependencies** | prose only; product-prover-pack:6 is the **only machine-readable one** (`requires: product-prover >= 1.3.0`) | 11/12 |
| **owner** | — | **absent across the board** (no skill names a maintainer) |
| **compatibility** | base-pin token in prose (the thing rules forbid); `metadata.version` only | no declared compat range in 11/12 |
| **fallback** | prose "Used standalone, this note is plain advice" in 10/12; text-audit:418 has a named "by-hand mode" | product-prover-pack, product-prover state none |
| **proof** | live-spec-base:16 (`tests/test_worker_restore.py`), spec-author (9 test refs), test-author (10), build-pipeline (5), publish (2) | communicator, feedback-intake, feedback-collector, text-audit, product-prover, product-prover-pack state **no proof mark** |

Systemically absent in every skill: **inputs, owner, machine-readable dependencies, compatibility range**. Half the pack has no proof mark.

## 1. PRODUCT_SPEC.md Req 170 / 171

**Req 170** (`/Users/sashaabramovich/live-spec/PRODUCT_SPEC.md:3908-3930`) — 7 criteria:
- `:3917` founding answers the questions in the new spec's opening before the first request
- `:3918` personal-tool-or-reusable-product asked first
- `:3920` **the blocking clause**: "*shall* block the first request until the system asks it or reads its answer from the profile; an ordinary open question rides along without stopping work, and this one *shall* not. [INV-4, INV-12, B-2]"
- `:3923` personal-scope standing preference seeds the default, said aloud
- `:3925` no standing preference ⇒ ask the human
- `:3926` **never-infer law**: no founding answer from example artifacts; naming three artifacts does not decide the product
- `:3930` adoption's orient puts the same questions, personal-versus-reusable first

**Req 171** (`:3934-3958`) — 9 criteria: find profile at its one home at founding/orient/new machine or human (`:3941`); load + name file + read unrecognized lines aloud (`:3942`); absent ⇒ offer from `templates/profile.template.md` (`:3943`); told lines written faithfully (`:3948`); **named-source line-by-line flow** at `:3951` — read the source, propose lines, accept or drop each one at a time on the human's word, "A dropped proposal *shall* stay dropped"; placeholders marked (`:3952`); decline ⇒ pack defaults, said aloud, offer returns at next project setup not mid-work (`:3955`); profile exists ⇒ skip and load (`:3956`); **`:3958` "A worker session *shall* onboard no one; its brief already carries the setting lines it needs. [ACT-3]"**

## 2. Implementation

- `/Users/sashaabramovich/live-spec/adopt/START.md:41-49` — Phase 1 "who is being worked for, and the founding questions"; profile read/offered first, then questions, done-when = every question in `scripts/founding-questions.json` answered or profile-read plus the economy rung. Host-profile write at `:81-93`. START never names personal-versus-reusable explicitly — it delegates to the JSON.
- `/Users/sashaabramovich/live-spec/adopt/ADOPT.md:100-142` — orient records kind, layers/proofs, design-principles, axes, config-surface, `founding.set-version`, economy rung, skill search, settings card.
- `/Users/sashaabramovich/live-spec/scripts/founding-questions.json` — real machine artifact, `set_version: 6`, 7 questions each with `since`/`anchor`/`key`.
- `/Users/sashaabramovich/live-spec/scripts/check-pack-update.sh:110-147,156-170` — INV-227 founding arm is genuinely wired: reads `founding.set-version` from the profile, names later questions, versionless host owes all, prints "PROPOSAL ONLY".

**Prose-only** (no machine enforcement anywhere): Req 170.3's blocking, 170.6's never-infer, all of Req 171 — the line-by-line accept/drop flow, "a dropped proposal shall stay dropped", the decline path, and the worker-never-onboards rule. Only string-presence tests guard them.

| M-408 (`:492`) | `tests/test_founding_set_version.py` | implemented + tested + installed + invoked; fixture hosts drive the real `check-pack-update.sh` arm; red-proof recorded at HEAD 573d8ea 2026-07-18 |

| M-517 (`:498`) | `tests/test_setup_entry.py:608+` | strongest evidence — real founding on a throwaway tree, first green, host keys only, second run preserves human text, placeholders red |

- `adopt/install-ratchet.sh:125-189`: `sha256_of`, manifest merged not rebuilt (:139-151), scaffold pins folded into the same manifest (:153-179), `pack_version` + `seeded` + `tier` written at :182-187.

- Offline evidence beyond the honest skip: **none.** No cached last-known-good remote VERSION, no staleness bound on the stamp, no offline mode in `install-external-skills.sh`.

Restore is a manual `cp`. The only "restore" discipline in the pack (`skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md:200`, INV-298) is about worker working-trees, not installed skills.
